name: Foreign Employee Work Permit and Carte d'Identité d'Étranger (CIE)

requirements.blocker_text: The Senegalese employer must submit the signed employment contract to the Directorate of Labor with a cover letter and sponsorship letter, generally including a 'certificat de non-disponibilité' showing no suitable local candidate was found, and enroll the worker in the CSS and IPRES social-security systems from day one. Formal labor directorate approval is required before work can begin (typically 2-4 weeks).
requirements.fix_path: Have the employer secure Directorate of Labor contract approval before starting work.

requirements.blocker_text: Must apply for the Carte d'Identité d'Étranger (CIE) at the Division de la Police des Étrangers (DPETV) within 90 days of arrival, including a medical exam and a repatriation deposit at the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (amount varies by nationality, e.g. ~USD 215 for US citizens). A renewable 6-month receipt is issued while the physical card (valid 5 years once issued) is processed, which can take 6-12 months.
requirements.fix_path: Apply for the CIE within 90 days of arrival and pay the repatriation deposit.

evidence_required.document: Signed employment contract from a Senegal-registered company
Medical certificate from a Senegalese physician

outcome.duration_length: initial contract 2 years (renewable); CIE card valid 5 years once physically issued

sources.title: Expat.com (private expatriate-guide site) -- Senegal work-permit process: Directorate of Labor contract approval, CSS/IPRES social security enrollment, CIE application via DPETV within 90 days, repatriation deposit, and 5-year CIE card validity once issued
